title: CEO Interview with Dr. Sean Wei of Easy-Logic
gist: Easy-Logic CEO Sean Wei presents EasylogicECO, a purpose-built Functional ECO tool that patches netlists late in ASIC design, as several times faster and producing patches about 30% better than ECO add-ons built on formal verification platforms. The Hong Kong company says it has nearly 100 paying customers and is adding AI engines (EasyAI ECO Suite) and more ECO types to build a full incremental design tool chain.

insights.claim: Industry data cited by Easy-Logic says more than 86% of ASICs need two or more tape-outs, and logic and functional problems are among the leading causes of tape-out failure. Re-running the full design flow for a late change can take months and cost millions of dollars.
insights.speaker: Sean Wei
insights.so_what: Re-spins are expensive, which supports demand for tools that make targeted late-stage logic fixes.
insights.quote: Industry data indicates that over 86% of ASICs require two or more tape-outs, with logic and functional issues among the leading causes of tape-out failure.

insights.claim: Because chips are getting more complex and schedules tighter, design teams can no longer assume RTL stays unchanged after freeze. ECO windows are often very short, sometimes just before tape-out or even after mask release, so speed and getting a good result on the first run matter most.
insights.speaker: Sean Wei
insights.so_what: Functional ECO is moving from an occasional fix to a routine need in complex SoC programs.

insights.claim: A functional ECO patch that is generated successfully can still cause trouble if it is too large. An oversized patch makes timing closure and physical implementation harder and can disturb scan chains, low-power structures and DFT constraints.
insights.speaker: Sean Wei
insights.so_what: Patch size, not just whether the ECO succeeds, decides whether an ECO tool actually saves the schedule.
insights.quote: Even when an ECO is generated successfully, an oversized patch can make timing closure and physical implementation difficult.
insights.locator: Second, backend implementation must still converge.

themes.theme: Purpose-built vs formal-verification add-on ECO tools

insights.claim: Most Functional ECO tools on the market are add-ons to formal verification platforms, and the underlying verification technology limits them: long runtimes, limited automation and poor usability. A tool built around ECO-specific algorithms avoids these limits.
insights.speaker: Sean Wei
insights.so_what: Easy-Logic is positioning itself against the ECO add-ons of the large EDA vendors that dominate the market.
insights.quote: Many existing Functional ECO tools are add-ons to formal verification platforms rather than purpose-built ECO tools.

insights.claim: Easy-Logic, founded in Hong Kong in 2013 out of the EDA lab at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, says it has nearly 100 paying customers across mainland China, Taiwan, the US and South Korea. It pitches itself as an ECO alternative that avoids depending on a single EDA vendor.

themes.theme: AI engines and incremental design roadmap

insights.claim: Easy-Logic's EasyAI ECO Suite adds AI engines to the ECO workflow. Auto Partition cuts patch size by more than 20% on average (up to 90%), Learning/I-Learning cuts patch size by more than 20% on average, and Smart Caching cuts runtime by up to 80% when runs are repeated.
insights.speaker: Sean Wei
insights.so_what: This is another example of AI-assisted EDA moving into narrow, high-value late-stage design steps.
insights.quote: Smart Caching reuses results from previous runs and can reduce runtime by up to 80% in multi-iteration scenarios.
insights.locator: We have introduced EasyAI ECO Suite

insights.claim: EasylogicECO currently supports Functional, Scan Chain, Low Power and Metal ECO. Easy-Logic is developing Clock Tree, Placement, Timing and Routing ECO, aiming for an incremental design tool chain that covers all late-stage chip changes.
insights.speaker: Sean Wei
insights.so_what: Easy-Logic is trying to grow from a single-point ECO tool into a broader backend incremental flow.
